title: SC scraps bond rule for seafarers claiming disputed awards
summary: The Supreme Court (SC) has declared unconstitutional and void the requirement for seafarers to post a bond before claiming disputed monetary awards and damages pending appeal or judicial review.

blocks.text: The Supreme Court (SC) has declared unconstitutional and void the requirement for seafarers to post a bond before claiming disputed monetary awards and damages pending appeal or judicial review.

In a press release issued Monday, the SC En Banc partially granted five consolidated petitions filed by seafarers, labor groups and maritime schools questioning provisions of Republic Act No. 12021, or the Magna Carta of Filipino Seafarers, as well as its implementing rules and related issuances.

Under Section 59 of the law, monetary awards for wages, statutory benefits and undisputed amounts were immediately executory. However, seafarers were required to post a bond before claiming disputed amounts and damages to guarantee repayment if the ruling was later overturned or modified.

The SC ruled that the bond requirement violated the constitutional guarantees of due process and equal protection by imposing a financial burden on seafarers seeking to enforce favorable labor judgments, a requirement not similarly imposed on other workers.

“The Court held that the bond requirement violated the Due Process and Equal Protection Clauses of the Constitution. It imposed a financial burden on seafarers seeking to enforce favorable labor judgments and subjected them to a disadvantage not similarly imposed on other workers,” the SC said.

“While recognizing the State’s interest in preventing ambulance chasing and protecting the maritime industry against unrestituted awards, the Court found that these objectives did not justify the challenged restriction on the execution of monetary awards,” it added.
Section 59 also allowed the Department of Migrant Workers’ Agarang Kalinga at Saklolo Para sa mga OFW na Nangangailangan (AKSYON) Fund to cover the bond premiums.

The SC likewise declared this provision unconstitutional, saying the use of public funds to pay private bond premiums violated Section 29(1), Article VI of the Constitution, which requires public money to be spent strictly for a public purpose.
The High Court also struck down provisions of Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) Department Order No. 247, Series of 2025, that enforced the bond requirement.
The SC emphasized, however, that the Magna Carta of Filipino Seafarers remains valid and enforceable, except for the provisions expressly declared unconstitutional or void.
“The law therefore remains valid and enforceable, except for the provisions expressly declared unconstitutional or void,” it said.
Associate Justice Maria Filomena Singh penned the decision. — MCG, GMA News
